patients.summary: Wildlife photographer who joined in 2022 with healed injuries from a 2019 collision. A 2024 collision left a CSF leak that settled with conservative care, a missed diaphragm injury presented and was repaired in January 2025, and after he was last seen in July 2025 an ICU admission for clinical rabies reached the practice only as a records request and an admission note.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 33 y/o man, moved his care here after his last doctor retired. Healthy, no chronic prescriptions, sees nobody regularly. Cigna OAP card info taken. Booked new patient visit 9/20 at 8:30. Membership packet and records release emailed.

conditions.label: History of mild traumatic brain injury

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
33M joining the practice. Previous PCP retired; records release signed today.

HPI: Feels well. No complaints today. Works as a wildlife photographer, lots of time outdoors and in the field, often hiking long distances with gear.

Past history: In August 2019 he was in a car crash. Was taken to a trauma center: several broken ribs, a bruised lung, and a mild brain injury, plus belly trauma that was watched and did not need an operation. Admitted a few days, no surgery. Ribs healed over a couple of months. Fully back to baseline since. No ongoing breathing problems.
Surgical: none.
Meds: multivitamin daily. No Rx.
Allergies: none to medications.
Family: father has high blood pressure, well controlled. No autoimmune disease or bleeding problems in the family.
Social: never smoked. 2-3 drinks/week, socially. No drug use. Lives with his male partner, monogamous. No tattoos, never had a transfusion. Thinks he had the hep B series as a kid or teen; no paperwork.
Immunizations: unsure of tetanus date, possibly at the trauma center. Will confirm from records.

ROS: negative except as above.

Exam: Vitals as recorded. Well-appearing, fit. HEENT: TMs clear, nares patent, oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no thyromegaly or nodes. Lungs clear, symmetric expansion, nontender chest wall. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Extremities no edema. Neuro: alert, oriented, CN II-XII intact, strength and gait normal. Skin: no rashes.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 2.

A/P:
1. Health maintenance, 33M. Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids today. HIV and hep C one-time screening offered and accepted. Flu and COVID boosters when the fall supply is in, nurse visit.
2. Remote multiple rib fractures, pulmonary contusion and mild TBI from 2019 collision, healed, no residual issues. Will review trauma records when they come.
3. Tdap status unclear, will check records before giving.
Follow up yearly, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Nathan, all of your bloodwork from Tuesday came back normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, sugar and cholesterol. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do here. We'll get you in for flu and COVID shots next month once the clinic has stock.

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Records from former primary care office, 2016 to 2022, 41 pages.

Contents: yearly wellness visits 2016-2021, normal exams and normal routine bloodwork. Medication list: multivitamin. Allergies: NKDA.

Included trauma center discharge summary, admission 08/10/2019 to 08/13/2019: restrained occupant in a motor vehicle collision. Injuries: multiple rib fractures, pulmonary contusion, mild traumatic brain injury, blunt abdominal trauma. Managed nonoperatively with pain control and incentive spirometry. Tdap given in the trauma bay 08/10/2019. Discharged home in stable condition with outpatient follow-up.

Post-crash PCP visit 09/2019: recovering as expected. Visit 11/2019: back to work, symptoms resolved.

Reviewed. Tdap 2019 entered into immunization record; not due until 2029.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for flu and bivalent COVID booster. Afebrile, no illness today. Flu to L deltoid, COVID to R deltoid. Lot numbers and VIS documented. Waited 15 min after, felt fine, left ambulatory.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. Busy summer, shooting a lot of bird migration work up north. Feels great. No chest pain, shortness of breath, headaches. Sleeping fine.

Meds: multivitamin. NKDA.
Social unchanged, still a few drinks a week, never smoker.

Exam: vitals as charted. Appears well. HEENT normal. Lungs clear. Heart RRR without murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Neuro grossly normal. Skin: sun-exposed, no concerning lesions seen; reminded about sunscreen and a hat in the field.

PHQ-2 0.

Plan: CMP and lipids today. Tdap current (2019). Flu and COVID next month. Recheck in a year.

documents.title: Travel shots?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hey doc, my partner and I are finally doing the big trip, about three months backpacking through Vietnam, Cambodia and Laos, leaving sometime in the spring. Lots of rural areas and some wildlife sanctuaries for work. What shots or pills do I need? Can you do that or do I go somewhere?

documents.title: RE: Travel shots?
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sounds like an amazing trip. For a long rural itinerary like that I'd like you to see the travel medicine clinic with infectious disease; they stock the travel vaccines and handle malaria and other region-specific advice. Referral sent. Their office should call you within a week or two. Bring whatever vaccine records you have.

documents.title: Travel Medicine Consultation
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Outside infectious disease / travel medicine clinic
Date of visit: 12/04/2023
Reason for referral: pre-travel advice, about 3 months of backpacking through Vietnam, Cambodia and Laos, departing spring 2024.

Thank you for sending this pleasant 35-year-old photographer. He will be traveling overland for roughly three months, mostly rural, with some time at wildlife reserves.

Past medical history: remote collision with healed rib fractures, a pulmonary contusion that resolved, and a mild TBI without residua. No surgeries.
Medications: multivitamin daily only.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father with treated hypertension; no autoimmune or bleeding disorders in the family.
Social: monogamous relationship with a male partner. Denies illicit drugs, prior transfusion or tattoos. Never smoker, light social alcohol.
Immunizations: reports a completed hepatitis B series in the past. No documentation of hepatitis A vaccine.

Exam: afebrile, vital signs within normal limits. General exam unremarkable.

Labs: liver function tests drawn today were normal.

Assessment: healthy traveler, not immune to hepatitis A by history, at risk on this itinerary.

Plan:
- Hepatitis A vaccine, dose 1 given today in clinic. Second dose due in 6 to 12 months; his primary care office can give it.
- Food and water precautions, insect avoidance, and traveler's diarrhea guidance reviewed with handouts.
- He will contact us if itinerary changes.

Allergies: NKDA. Copy to referring primary care physician.

documents.title: Consult letter filed
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Travel clinic letter received by fax, scanned. Hep A #1 (12/4/23) added to immunization history. Second dose reminder set for summer 2024.

conditions.label: Cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhea
conditions.note: after minor collision in late January 2024

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional emergency department
Date of service: 02/18/2024

CC: watery drip from the right side of the nose x 2 weeks.

HPI: 35M, history of a 2019 collision with rib fractures, lung contusion and mild TBI. About three weeks ago he was in a low-speed car accident and had a mild concussion; he did not go to a hospital for it. For the last two weeks he has had a thin, clear drip from the right nostril only. It runs more when he leans forward to tie his boots and when he bears down on the toilet. No cold symptoms, no seasonal allergies, no stuffiness.

PMH: as above, plus not immune to hepatitis A (travel clinic 12/2023). PSH: none. Meds: multivitamin. Allergies: NKDA. FHx: father with hypertension; no autoimmune or bleeding disorders. SHx: never smoker, 2-3 drinks/wk, wildlife photographer.

Exam: afebrile, vitals normal. Nonfocal neurologic exam. Anterior rhinoscopy: clear fluid from the right naris, mucosa without redness or swelling, no polyps or mass. Head and neck otherwise normal.

Labs: serum glucose 98 mg/dL. Nasal fluid glucose 60 mg/dL, nasal fluid protein elevated. Nasal fluid sent for beta-2 transferrin.

MDM: unilateral clear rhinorrhea after head trauma with glucose-containing fluid, concerning for CSF leak. No fever or meningeal signs. Discussed with patient.

Disposition: home. Head of bed up, no nose blowing, avoid straining and heavy lifting, return for fever, stiff neck, worsening headache or confusion. Follow up with PCP in 2-3 days and ENT.

Addendum 02/21/2024: beta-2 transferrin POSITIVE. Patient called with result. Diagnosis: CSF rhinorrhea.

Allergies: NKDA. Copy to primary care.

documents.title: ED record filed
documents.author: MA
documents.body: ED record with 2/21 addendum received by fax and scanned. Routed to PCP; patient already seen 2/21.

documents.title: ER yesterday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Morning. I ended up in the ER yesterday because my right nostril has been dripping clear water for two weeks, ever since a fender bender at the end of January. They think it might be spinal fluid and sent a test. They said see you this week. Is that a big deal? I bumped my head in the crash but didn't think much of it.

documents.title: RE: ER yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know. Usually these settle on their own, but we take them seriously. Front desk will put you in Wednesday morning. Until then keep doing what the ER said: no blowing your nose, no heavy lifting or straining. If you get a fever, a stiff neck or a bad headache, go straight back to the ER.

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth twice daily to keep stools soft

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Seen in the ER Sunday for two weeks of clear right-sided nasal drip after a minor car accident around 1/28 in which he hit his head (mild concussion, did not seek care at the time). Drip continues, worse leaning forward. No fever, no headache, no neck stiffness, no vision change. Concussion symptoms were brief and are gone. ER called him this morning: beta-2 transferrin came back positive.

Meds: multivitamin. NKDA.

O: vitals as charted, afebrile. Alert, conversant. Clear thin fluid at right naris, more with head forward. Neck supple. CN II-XII intact, strength symmetric, gait normal. Lungs clear, heart regular.

A/P: Traumatic CSF rhinorrhea, confirmed by beta-2 transferrin.
- Most of these close with conservative care; ENT referral placed (urgent) for skull base evaluation and imaging.
- Head of bed raised, no nose blowing, sneeze with mouth open, nothing heavy, no straining.
- Docusate 100 mg twice daily so he doesn't strain.
- Meningitis warning signs reviewed again: fever, stiff neck, worsening headache, confusion -> ER.
- He had planned to leave on a long trip this spring; advised holding off until ENT clears him.

documents.title: Referral scheduled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: ENT office confirmed receipt of referral. Pt scheduled with them 3/4 at 10:15. Pt notified by phone, verbalized understanding.

reports.study: CT sinuses without contrast, thin section
reports.text:
Technique: thin-section axial CT of the paranasal sinuses and anterior skull base without contrast, with coronal and sagittal reformats.

Findings: No fracture of the anterior skull base, cribriform plate, ethmoid roof, sphenoid sinus walls or frontal sinus. No pneumocephalus. No discrete bony defect is identified to localize a leak. Paranasal sinuses are clear and well aerated. Nasal septum midline. Osteomeatal units patent. Visualized orbits and intracranial contents unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: No skull base fracture or pneumocephalus. Leak site not localized.

documents.title: Otolaryngology Consultation
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside otolaryngology group
Date of visit: 03/04/2024

Reason: CSF rhinorrhea after head trauma, referred by PCP.

History: 35M with clear right-sided rhinorrhea since early February, starting about a week after a minor car accident with mild concussion. Positive beta-2 transferrin from the ED on 2/18. No fever, meningismus or visual symptoms. Drainage is somewhat less over the past week. Using docusate, sleeping with head elevated.
PMH: remote multitrauma 2019 (healed rib fractures, resolved pulmonary contusion, mild TBI). Meds: multivitamin, docusate. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: afebrile. Nasal endoscopy: small amount of clear fluid on the right with head-down positioning, mucosa healthy, no mass. Neuro grossly intact.

Imaging: thin-section sinus CT today shows no skull base fracture or pneumocephalus; site not localized.

Impression: post-traumatic CSF rhinorrhea, low volume and improving.

Plan: continue conservative management (head elevation, stool softener, no nose blowing or heavy lifting). Most post-traumatic leaks close within weeks. Recheck in four weeks; if still leaking, further localization would be considered. Travel and flying deferred until then.

Allergies: NKDA. Copy to primary care.

documents.title: Otolaryngology Follow-up
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside otolaryngology group
Date of visit: 04/01/2024

Follow-up of post-traumatic CSF rhinorrhea. Drainage stopped completely around the middle of March and has not returned, including with bending and exertion. No fever or headache.

Exam: nasal endoscopy shows no fluid at rest or with head-down positioning. Mucosa normal.

Impression: post-traumatic CSF leak, resolved with conservative care.

Plan: may resume normal activity gradually. Cleared to fly and travel. Stop stool softener. Return for any recurrence of clear drainage, and seek urgent care for fever, stiff neck or severe headache.

Allergies: NKDA. Copy to primary care.

documents.title: Late letter filed
documents.author: MA
documents.body: ENT follow-up letter from 4/1/24 received today after records request. Scanned and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Cleared!
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw ENT yesterday. The drip stopped mid March and they said it's healed, I'm cleared to fly. They told me to stop the stool softener. We leave next week for the trip, back around early July. Do I need anything else before I go?

documents.title: RE: Cleared!
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news. Nothing else from us before you leave; the travel clinic covered you. Your second hepatitis A shot is due this summer, so we'll give it at your physical when you're back. If the clear drip ever comes back, call ENT right away. Safe travels.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: No ENT letter from the 4/1 follow-up in chart. Called ENT office, requested visit note be faxed. They will send.

documents.body:

events.reason: sudden shortness of breath and left chest pain

conditions.label: Traumatic diaphragmatic hernia
conditions.note: left-sided, delayed presentation of 2019 blunt trauma

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain
Take 2 tablets by mouth every 8 hours as needed for pain

reports.text: Single upright AP view of the chest. The left hemidiaphragm is elevated, and gas-filled loops of bowel project over the left lower and mid thorax. The mediastinum is shifted toward the right. The right lung is clear. No pneumothorax.
reports.conclusion: Elevated left hemidiaphragm with bowel loops in the left hemithorax and rightward mediastinal shift, consistent with diaphragmatic hernia.

reports.text: CT chest with IV contrast, including the upper abdomen. There is a defect in the left hemidiaphragm through which loops of bowel herniate into the left thorax, with rightward mediastinal shift. Herniated bowel enhances normally; no free air or pneumatosis. No pleural effusion. No pneumothorax. Heart size normal.
reports.conclusion: Left diaphragmatic defect with herniated bowel into the left chest and mediastinal shift. Bowel enhancement preserved.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Hospital emergency department
Date of service: 01/17/2025

CC: abrupt shortness of breath and pain on the left side of the chest.

HPI: 36M, photographer, with a past collision that broke several ribs and bruised his lung. This afternoon he became suddenly short of breath with left chest pain. No fever or cough.

PMH (per prior records): hepatitis A susceptibility, CSF rhinorrhea, healed rib fractures, resolved pulmonary contusion, mild TBI. PSH: none. Meds: multivitamin. Allergies: NKDA. FHx: father HTN; no autoimmune or bleeding disorders. SHx: never smoker, social alcohol 2-3/week.

Vitals on arrival: BP 130/85, HR 105, RR 22, SpO2 92% on room air.
Exam: breath sounds diminished over the left chest, tympanic to percussion on that side. Right chest clear. Abdomen soft.

Labs: CBC and chemistries within normal limits.
Upright CXR: elevated left hemidiaphragm, bowel loops in the left chest, mediastinum pushed to the right.
CT chest: left diaphragmatic defect with herniated bowel, enhancement preserved.

Assessment: traumatic diaphragmatic hernia, presenting late after prior blunt trauma.

Plan: NG decompression, supplemental oxygen, general surgery consulted, admitted to surgery for repair.

Allergies: NKDA. Copy to primary care.

documents.title: Operative Report
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Hospital general surgery
Date of operation: 01/18/2025

Preoperative diagnosis: left traumatic diaphragmatic hernia.
Postoperative diagnosis: same.
Procedure: laparoscopic reduction of hernia contents and primary repair of left diaphragm.
Anesthesia: general endotracheal.

Findings: defect in the left hemidiaphragm with herniated bowel loops into the left chest. Contents reduced without difficulty; bowel pink, peristalsing and viable throughout, no resection needed. Defect closed primarily with interrupted nonabsorbable sutures. Left chest re-expanded under positive pressure; no chest tube needed.

EBL minimal. No complications. To recovery in stable condition.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Hospital general surgery
Admitted 01/17/2025, discharged 01/21/2025.

Diagnosis: traumatic left diaphragmatic hernia, delayed presentation.
Procedure: laparoscopic reduction and primary repair 01/18/2025.

Course: presented through the ED with acute dyspnea and left chest pain; imaging showed bowel in the left chest. Repaired the next morning. Oxygen weaned off on postoperative day 1, diet advanced, ambulating, pain controlled on oral medication. Discharged home on hospital day 5.

Discharge medications: oxycodone 5 mg every 6 hours as needed (#12), acetaminophen 1000 mg every 8 hours as needed, home multivitamin.
Instructions: no lifting over 10 lb for six weeks; may shower; surgical clinic follow-up in about three weeks.

Allergies: NKDA. Copy to primary care physician.

documents.title: Hospital records filed
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Operative report and discharge summary for January admission received today after second request. Scanned and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Home from hospital
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called. Was admitted Fri 1/17 with a diaphragm hernia, had laparoscopic surgery Sat, discharged yesterday. Pain manageable, using the oxycodone mostly at night plus Tylenol. Breathing comfortably, no fever, eating. Pharmacy fill history shows oxycodone 5 mg #12 filled 1/21. No hospital paperwork here yet. Scheduled post-hospital visit 1/29. Advised ER for fever, worsening shortness of breath or vomiting.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-discharge visit. Admitted 1/17 to 1/21 for a left diaphragmatic hernia, felt to be from the 2019 crash, missed at the time. Laparoscopic repair 1/18 per patient and ED record (received 1/24); op note and discharge summary not yet received.

Now: soreness at the port sites, improving. Stopped the oxycodone 2 days ago, using acetaminophen occasionally. No shortness of breath, cough, fever, nausea or vomiting. Bowels moving normally. Walking a few miles a day.

Meds: multivitamin, acetaminophen as needed. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted, SpO2 normal on room air. Comfortable. Breath sounds equal bilaterally, no tympany. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender near port sites, incisions clean and dry, no erythema or drainage.

A/P: s/p laparoscopic repair of traumatic diaphragmatic hernia, recovering as expected.
- Lifting limit 10 lb until early March per surgery.
- Surgical follow-up already scheduled.
- Records request sent to hospital for op note and discharge summary.
- Call for fever, worsening pain, shortness of breath.

documents.title: Surgeon visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw the surgeon yesterday. All healed, he's happy. Still no lifting heavy camera stuff until early March and then I can go back to normal. FYI in case you don't get a letter.

documents.title: RE: Surgeon visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks, Nathan, good to hear. Noted in your chart.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly exam, rescheduled from 6/26. Fully back to work and hiking with full packs since March. No chest pain, shortness of breath, reflux or bowel trouble since the January surgery. No nasal drainage. No headaches.

Meds: multivitamin. NKDA.
Social: never smoker; a few drinks a week. Same partner, same work.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight back to his usual. Well. Nares clear. Lungs clear with equal breath sounds both bases. Heart RRR. Abdomen soft, nontender, port scars well healed. No hernia at port sites. Neuro nonfocal.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P:
1. Annual preventive: CBC, CMP, lipids today.
2. Traumatic diaphragmatic hernia, repaired 1/2025: healed, no symptoms. Resolving on problem list.
3. Hep A series complete 2024. Tdap good to 2029. Flu and COVID this fall.
RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Call from hospital ICU
documents.author: RN
documents.body: ICU nurse at an outside hospital called. Patient admitted to their ICU overnight; they are asking for his immunization history, specifically any rabies vaccine. Reviewed our record: no rabies vaccine ever documented. Hep A x2 (12/2023, 8/2024), Tdap 8/2019, flu and COVID per record. Immunization record faxed to the ICU. PCP notified.

documents.title: PCP note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Aware. Asked ICU to send admission records.

documents.title: ICU Admission Note
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
Outside hospital medical ICU
Date of admission: 11/23/2025

CC: fever, headache and confusion for two days; tingling around an old scratch on the left forearm.

HPI: 37M. History of traumatic injuries including rib fractures, pulmonary contusion, mild TBI and a diaphragmatic hernia. Two days of fever and headache, now confused. He describes pins-and-needles around a healed wound on the left forearm. He remembers a bat scratching him there about two months ago while camping; he did not seek care at the time.

PMH (outside list): hepatitis A susceptibility, CSF rhinorrhea, traumatic diaphragmatic hernia, healed rib fractures, resolved pulmonary contusion, mild TBI. PSH: none listed. Home meds: multivitamin daily. Allergies: NKDA. FHx: father with treated hypertension; no autoimmune or bleeding disorders. SHx: never smoker, social alcohol, wildlife photographer.

Vitals: T 38.9 C, HR 110, BP 145/90.
Exam: agitated. Excess salivation; difficulty swallowing when offered water. Hyperreflexic. Encephalopathic. Healed scratch on left forearm; no other wounds or signs of infection.

Labs: WBC 11.0, Hgb 14.2, Plt 250. Na 135, K 4.0, BUN 14, Cr 1.0, glucose 98. CSF: lymphocytic pleocytosis, glucose and protein normal.

Assessment: clinical rabies, symptomatic phase, after bat exposure.

Plan: ICU admission, precautions and supportive care. Rabies diagnostics (saliva, serum, CSF, nuchal skin biopsy) sent to the state public health laboratory, results pending.

Allergies: NKDA. Copy to primary care physician.
